newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HBG says almost all units boosted profit.
newsitem.headline: HBG says almost all units boosted profit.

text.p: Dutch builder and dredger Hollandsche Beton Groep (HBG) said on Tuesday ordinary profits had been boosted by a modest upturn in almost all activities, a reduced tax burden and lower restructuring costs.

"The rise in profits from ordinary operations was generated across almost all activities," chairman Nic de Ronde Bresser said, signalling a recovery in European building operations, most of which broke even or posted losses last year.
HBG earlier reported first-half net profit from ordinary operations jumped by 21 percent to 57 million guilders, outstripping analysts' forecasts of 38-48.5 million guilders.
Investors cheered the news and the shares stood 9.50 guilders higher at 315.50 guilders at around 1025 GMT.
Net profit slipped two million guilders to 53 million due to a four million guilder net extraordinary charge compared with a net 15 million guilder gain in the same 1995 half.
De Ronde Bresser said the charge reflected restructuring costs at HBG's German subsidiary Raulf Bau-GmbH, which remained loss-making in the first half.
Raulf, hit by the sector-wide slump in Germany, was being slimmed down by "several hundred" jobs in order to improve margins, finance director Dick Sinninghe Damste said.
Also loss-making was HCG, HBG's process installations and equipment manufacturing subsidiary. However the company was expected to contribute to profits in 1997, he added.
Sinninghe Damste said dredging unit HAM had continued to perform well and its contribution to profits (estimated by analysts at some 35 percent) had again been "substantial".
But he added that its profit growth had lagged the rise across the group as a whole.
"The rise in profits from ordinary operations was generated mainly by activities other than dredging," he said.

"Last year we were very dependent on dredging and income from operations outside Europe, but profit growth in the first half was generated less by these activities and more by our other operations," he said.
HBG, which is active in the civil engineering, general building, road-building, housing and dredging sectors, derives 75 percent of turnover in the Netherlands, Britain and Germany.

Chairman Nic de Ronde Bresser said the Dutch market was developing reasonably well overall, while the company's U.K. subsidiaries -- Kyle Stewart, Edmund Nuttall and GA -- were holding up well in a difficult market.
However the German market remained a difficult market and was likely to deteriorate further, De Ronde Bresser said.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000.
